analysis.problem_summary: Determine if any element appears at least twice in an integer array.
analysis.intuition: By keeping track of elements encountered so far in a hash set, we can check whether the current element was seen before in linear time.
approach: Initialize an empty HashSet of integers.
Iterate through each number in the array.
Check if the HashSet already contains the current number; if it does, return true immediately.
Otherwise, add the number to the set and continue.
If the loop finishes without finding any duplicate, return false.
analysis.why_it_works: A HashSet stores unique elements and provides O(1) average lookup time. Finding an element already present in the set guarantees the existence of a duplicate.
analysis.key_takeaway: Using a hash set trades extra O(n) memory to achieve optimal linear O(n) execution time.
analysis.time_explanation: We iterate through the array of n elements once. Adding and searching in a HashSet takes O(1) average time per operation, giving an overall O(n) time complexity.
analysis.space_explanation: In the worst-case scenario where all elements are unique, the HashSet stores all n elements, consuming O(n) space.

analysis.problem_summary: Determine if any element appears at least twice in an integer array.
analysis.intuition: If the array is sorted, any duplicate values must land adjacent to one another. Sorting simplifies the duplicate check to scanning neighboring elements.
approach: Sort the array in ascending order using Arrays.sort().
Iterate through the array from index 0 up to n - 2.
Compare each element with its immediate neighbor (nums[i] == nums[i + 1]).
If any pair of adjacent elements are equal, return true.
If no matching adjacent pair is found after scanning the entire array, return false.
analysis.why_it_works: Sorting reorders the elements monotonically, bringing all instances of equal values adjacent to each other. Comparing neighboring elements is therefore sufficient to detect duplicates.
analysis.key_takeaway: Sorting avoids using extra heap space for hash structures at the expense of increasing time complexity to O(n log n).
analysis.time_explanation: Sorting the array dominates the runtime at O(n log n) time. The subsequent linear scan takes O(n) time, resulting in total time complexity of O(n log n).
analysis.space_explanation: Java's Arrays.sort() for primitive arrays uses Dual-Pivot Quicksort, requiring O(log n) auxiliary stack space.
